recipes.name: Super Easy Chicken and Dumplings
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.5 ounce) cans condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Stir condensed soup, chicken broth, and shredded chicken together in a large saucepan over medium-high heat until it begins to simmer.
Cut each biscuit into quarters, and gently stir into the simmering soup.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until biscuits are no longer doughy in the center, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Super Easy Chicken and Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: This hearty chicken and dumplings soup could not be simpler to make in one pot with easy ingredients for a comforting meal that tastes great!

video.description: In this video, we show you how to make a comforting and delicious dish of chicken and dumplings. This recipe is super easy to make, and it only requires a few simple ingredients. You only need cream of chicken soup, chicken broth, cooked chicken, and biscuit dough. This easy and delicious recipe is sure to become a family favorite.

review.reviewBody: Good. Did you know you can cut flour tortillas into strips for noodles?...Like homemade?

These were the best chicken and dumplings i ever made! I flattened my biscuits out thinner, cut them into smaller pieces and dusted them with flour to help them not stick together and it also helps thicken the gravy a little more. Absolutely delicious, super quick and easy. I also used rotisserie chicken already cooked.

This is the best base recipe! I’ve always made the crockpot version, but this is just as good—if not better—and it’s ready in a fraction of the time. Feel free to add any additional ingredients you like in your soup. I start by sautéing diced onion, celery, carrots, and garlic. After the biscuits are finished, I add a bag of frozen peas. I make sure to turn off the heat before adding the peas. For the chicken, I sear each side for two minutes, then add about half a cup of chicken broth. I cover the pan and cook the chicken for 10 minutes. Once it’s cooked, I shred the hot chicken with two forks and transfer it, along with the juices from the pan, to another pot while I prepare the rest of the dish.

This was very good with a couple tweaks. I used rotisserie chicken breast and to give it more flavor, I added a tsp. of chicken Better Than Bouillon as well as some pepper and a splash of heavy cream and a pinch of fresh thyme.I also added some frozen peas and carrots. The broth was a bit thin for my liking so I stirred in a tsp of cornstarch mixed with a tbsp of cold water when cooking was complete. Finish off with a sprinkling of freshly chopped parsley. Fast and delicious! The next time I make this, I plan on starting with sautéing finely chopped onion and celery until soft and light brown.

I used a whole 48oz of chicken broth,2 10oz cans of cream of chicken. Also I like mine thicker so I added 4 teaspoons of cornstarch. Added 3 chicken cubes. And used only 1 can of buttery jumbo biscuits, flattened & cut into 8, they cooked so better in smaller peices. For the chicken I bought already pulled rotisserie chicken from Walmart. I used shaved carrots & added Italian, Organo & pepper. Super easy & very good!

This was a fantastic place to start for an easy chicken and dumplings. THB I started with a mirepoix, fresh garlic, and some herbs, deglazed with a bourbon then followed the recipe as is. Came out amazingly good. Thanks for the base recipe and it’s easily adapted to one’s preferences.

Everything is perfect except the best thing to do is boil your chicken with onion and celery. Use that broth rather than the store bought chicken broth and it's AMAZING!!!! The flavor is so much better!!! But this is quick and easy and I recommend 10/10.

I’m versed in the kitchen but have never made chicken and dumplings. This was my first time. I did thicken it just a touch with corn starch- just remember to add the corn starch to a small amount of cold water then whisk it in briskly into your simmering pot. I don’t like store bought biscuits, so I used my grandmas drop biscuit recipe. Everything was perfect and flavorful, super tender meat and biscuits. I did add a bag of frozen peas and diced carrots before I added the biscuits let that simmer for 3 mins. My husband, kids, and kids that were guests as we were having a sleep over, had seconds and repeatedly said it was good

Super yum! 5 stars because it truly was easy. I halved the recipe because I only had 1 can of cream of chicken and it turned out great. I did add the full amount of chicken stock though since my biscuits were the grands version. I also added carrots, bunch of seasonings (pepper, dried parsley, minced onion, oregano, and a dash of chili flakes), as well as sauteing the chicken in bacon fat (since I had it left from breakfast that AM). I also cut the chicken into cubes before sauteing and just added everything to the pan after. I suggest using a Dutch oven or larger pot if you go the extra liquid route.

I made this last night after reading some of the comments saying that it needed some seasoning. I cooked my chicken in the crockpot with salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, basil and one can of chicken broth. I shredded it, then added the cooking liquid and an additional can of broth to a Dutch oven with the shredded chicken, one can of cream of chicken soup and one can of cream of celery soup to give it a little celery flavor (my husband doesn't like chunks of celery in things.) I took the biscuits and rolled each one fairly thin, then cut them up and put them in the simmering broth and cooked them for about 12 - 14 minutes. It was very good and I will make it again.
Super quick, easy and delicious! I sautéed some onions and carrots before adding broth and soup. I also added a can of cream of celery and my family loves it!

No need for so much cream of chicken. It will just make your soup taste like campbells. Use white wings flour tortilla mix, or any other flour tortilla mix for your dumplings. Season the flour with a little garlic powder and pepper. Prepare following directions on tortilla mix, except no need to rest or knead to much. No need to roll. Pull pieces of the dough and throw them in the pot for 10 min to simmer
I add frozen peas and carrots .

Followed the recipe. I tweaked just a little by adding 1 tsp of Caldo De Pollo Chicken Bouillon. I also flattened my biscuit dough and after cutting into small sizes I sprinkled generously with onion powder and patted into the dough. I also thickened just a tad with cornstarch flurry. It was delicious and I will def make again, I’m sure a lot as my husband raved about it.
My second time making it. It’s good!

I added carrots, celery and onion to the soup and chicken and let it cook. I then added some cornstarch and water to the soup to thicken it. Put flour on the biscuits and let it cook for 20-25 minutes. It was delish. Almost like a chicken pot pie soup. Family favorite. Definitely will make again.

This was an easy to follow recipe. I took the liberty added chopped onions, bell peppers and celery to the broth mixture. It gave the dumplings much flavor and punch. I'll probably try this again. Thanks
I used 2 cans of Pillsbury croissants cut into strips for the dumplings. They were perfect. My husband and I really loved the chicken and dumplings.
I made this, and it was awful. Biscuit dough was like bubble gum. Sorry.

Followed recipe. But needed to be thickened and dumplings needed to cook longer. Added a bit of cornstarch slurry to thicken snd increased cook time if biscuits to about 30 min and voila. Absolutely yummy. Will make again and again
